_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written from scratch.
name: Kavita
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Kavita is a reading server for comics, manga and ebooks, with a web reader and OPDS for reading apps. The egg creates the admin account with a password made at install and turns off its usage statistics.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Kavita: downloads Kavita from its GitHub releases, checked against
# GitHub's checksum, into kavita/. Kavita's database, settings and covers
# live in config/ (kavita/config points there) and the books in library/;
# neither is ever touched. The app is only replaced once the new one has
# downloaded and unpacked.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=Kareadita/Kavita
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# gh_tag <latest|tag> prints the release's tag; returns 1 when there's no
# such release, 2 when GitHub can't be reached.
gh_tag() {
    local out
    out=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$1" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; return 0; }
    case "$out" in *"has no release"* | *"no releases"*) return 1 ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
}
offline="GitHub can't be reached right now, or is limiting downloads. Reinstall to try again in a few minutes."
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Kavita has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
case "$version" in latest|v*) ;; *) version="v$version" ;; esac
rc=0; tag=$(gh_tag "$version") || rc=$?
if [ "$rc" = 1 ]; then
    latest=$(gh_tag latest) || fail "$offline"
    fail "Kavita has no version ${VERSION}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as ${latest#v}."
fi
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || fail "$offline"
version=$tag
asset="kavita-linux-$arch.tar.gz"
assets=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$version") || fail "$offline"
sum=$(awk -v a="$asset" '$1 == a { print $2 }' <<<"$assets")
[ -n "$sum" ] || fail "Kavita $version has no Linux build for this CPU. Choose another version."

tmp=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$tmp" .raptor-old && mkdir -p "$tmp"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp" .raptor-old' EXIT
mkdir -p config library
if [ -x kavita/Kavita ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-kavita 2>/dev/null)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "Kavita $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Kavita $version"
    gh-release download "$repo" "$version" "$asset" "$tmp/kavita.tar.gz" || fail "The download failed or didn't match GitHub's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    tar -xzf "$tmp/kavita.tar.gz" -C "$tmp"
    rm -f "$tmp/kavita.tar.gz"
    # The release is packed without the executable bit.
    [ -f "$tmp/Kavita/Kavita" ] && chmod +x "$tmp/Kavita/Kavita" || fail "Kavita $version's download doesn't have the server in it. Choose another version."
    # The first run's settings, for a new server only.
    [ -f config/appsettings.json ] || cp -n "$tmp/Kavita/config/appsettings-init.json" config/
    rm -rf "$tmp/Kavita/config"
    ln -s ../config "$tmp/Kavita/config"
    [ ! -e kavita ] || mv kavita .raptor-old
    mv "$tmp/Kavita" kavita
    echo "$sum" > .raptor-kavita
fi

# A new Kavita lets whoever opens it first create the admin account, and
# sends usage statistics to its developers. On the first install, start it
# once here (with its internet access blocked, so nothing is sent) to create
# the admin with a random password and turn the statistics off.
if [ ! -f config/kavita.db ]; then
    password="$(head -c 15 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=')A1!"
    port=15000
    base=config/appsettings.json
    [ -f "$base" ] || base=config/appsettings-init.json
    jq --argjson p "$port" '.Port = $p' "$base" > "$tmp/appsettings.json"
    mv -f "$tmp/appsettings.json" config/appsettings.json
    rm -f config/appsettings-init.json
    (cd kavita && HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 \
        DOTNET_SYSTEM_GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT=1 exec ./Kavita) > "$tmp/first.log" 2>&1 &
    pid=$!
    api="http://127.0.0.1:$port/api"
    # Requests to Kavita itself go through /usr/bin/curl: the install's curl
    # counts every refused connection as a failed download, and Kavita takes
    # a while to start listening (longer on ARM).
    lcurl=/usr/bin/curl
    up=0
    for _ in $(seq 300); do
        if $lcurl -fs -o /dev/null "$api/health"; then up=1; break; fi
        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
        sleep 1
    done
    ok=0
    if [ "$up" = 1 ] && user=$($lcurl -fsS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$(jq -n --arg p "$password" '{username: "admin", email: "", password: $p}')" "$api/account/register"); then
        token=$(jq -r .token <<<"$user")
        settings=$($lcurl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" "$api/settings") &&
            $lcurl -fsS -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $token" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d "$(jq '.allowStatCollection = false' <<<"$settings")" "$api/settings" && ok=1
    fi
    running=0; kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && running=1
    # (A job started in the background ignores SIGINT, so it's SIGTERM.)
    kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$pid" || true
    if [ "$ok" != 1 ]; then
        tail -n 30 "$tmp/first.log"
        rm -f config/kavita.db*
        if [ "$up" = 1 ]; then
            fail "Kavita started but refused to create its admin account (see above). Reinstall to try again."
        elif [ "$running" = 1 ]; then
            fail "Kavita didn't start answering within 5 minutes, so its admin account couldn't be created. Reinstall to try again."
        else
            fail "Kavita stopped while starting (see above), so its admin account couldn't be created. Reinstall to try again."
        fi
    fi
    echo "The admin account is admin, with the password $password. Change it in Kavita's settings."
fi
echo "Installed Kavita $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Kavita version to install, such as 0.9.1.4, or latest.
